title: Review mutable-reference interfaces
why: A mutable-reference parameter allows changes to the caller's object. Output and in/out references are idiomatic C++; this advisory asks for an interface review, not an automatic defect finding.
suggestion: Check that mutation and ownership are clear at the call site. Keep intentional output or in/out references; use a const reference or a returned result only when that better expresses the contract.
limitations: Lexical review of named lvalue-reference parameters in simple void, int, bool, and auto function signatures; aliases, custom return types, function-pointer parameters, nested parentheses, and macro-generated declarations may be missed.

Const qualification is checked on the referenced object, not unrelated parameters or nested template arguments. Types and overloads are not resolved, so declaration/expression ambiguities and const-qualified aliases cannot always be distinguished.
Does not infer whether a parameter is actually mutated or whether an output or in/out interface is appropriate.

One advisory per rule and file, located at the first matching parameter line; related_files preserves every other distinct matching source line. The count describes evidence lines, not defects or individual parameters.
